anchorData: Conventions for all numbers: g = 10 N/kg, so weight = mass x 10. Bucket plus water = 20 kg, weight 200 N. Well: water surface is the 0 m reference level; ground level (top of the well) is 8 m above it. The bucket is lifted 8 m at a steady speed in 20 s, so its KE does not change and the whole energy gain is PE. PE gained = 200 N x 8 m = 1600 J (same for every method). BUCKET PE TABLE (m = 20 kg): height 0 m = 0 J; 2 m = 400 J; 4 m = 800 J; 6 m = 1200 J; 8 m = 1600 J. DIRECT LIFT BY HAND: effort 200 N, distance 8 m, work = 1600 J, time 20 s, power = 80 W. PULLEY SYSTEM (one fixed pulley fixed above the well plus one movable pulley on the bucket hook; 2 rope sections support the bucket; mass of rope and movable pulley ignored): rope pulled 16 m for the bucket to rise 8 m; actual effort = 125 N; work input = 125 N x 16 m = 2000 J; useful work output = 1600 J; energy wasted to friction as heat (and a little sound) = 2000 J - 1600 J = 400 J; efficiency = 1600/2000 = 80%; time 20 s, so input power = 2000/20 = 100 W and useful output power = 1600/20 = 80 W. Ideal pulley (no friction): effort 100 N, MA = 2, VR = 2. Actual: MA = 200/125 = 1.6, VR = 16/8 = 2, efficiency = MA/VR = 1.6/2 = 80%. A single fixed pulley alone: VR = 1, ideal effort 200 N, it only changes direction of the force (a child can pull down using body weight). FREE-FALL TABLE (bucket released from 8 m, no losses, falling to the water): height 8 m: PE 1600 J, KE 0 J, v = 0; 6 m: PE 1200 J, KE 400 J, v = 6.3 m/s; 4 m: PE 800 J, KE 800 J, v = 8.9 m/s; 2 m: PE 400 J, KE 1200 J, v = 11.0 m/s; 0 m: PE 0 J, KE 1600 J, v = 12.6 m/s (v = sqrt(2gh), KE = 1/2 x 20 x v squared). REAL FALL (Lesson 4): measured speed at the water is 11 m/s, so KE = 1/2 x 20 x 121 = 1210 J; energy shared to heat, sound and air/rope friction = 1600 - 1210 = 390 J. PENDULUM (Lesson 2-3): bob 0.5 kg raised 0.2 m: PE at top = 0.5 x 10 x 0.2 = 1 J; speed at the bottom = 2 m/s; KE at bottom = 1/2 x 0.5 x 4 = 1 J. ROLLER COASTER (Lesson 2): car 1000 kg at top 20 m above bottom: PE = 200 000 J; at the bottom v = 20 m/s and KE = 1/2 x 1000 x 400 = 200 000 J (ideal, no friction). WORK SIGNS (Lesson 5): woman lifting bucket 8 m at steady speed: work by her = +1600 J; work by gravity = -1600 J; net work = 0 J. Lowering the bucket 8 m slowly by rope: work by woman = -1600 J; work by gravity = +1600 J. FRICTION AND POWER (Lesson 7): sack of maize 50 kg (weight 500 N) dragged 10 m at steady speed. Rough dirt ground: friction 150 N, work = 1500 J, time 25 s, power = 60 W. Smooth concrete floor: friction 100 N, work = 1000 J, time 20 s, power = 50 W. Stair climb: learner 50 kg climbs 20 steps of 0.15 m = 3 m height; work = 500 N x 3 m = 1500 J; walking time 6 s gives P = 250 W; running time 3 s gives P = 500 W. OTHER MACHINES (Lesson 8): ramp: 50 kg sack (500 N) loaded onto a lorry 1.0 m high using a 4 m plank; actual effort 200 N; work in = 200 x 4 = 800 J; work out = 500 x 1 = 500 J; VR = 4; MA = 500/200 = 2.5; efficiency = 2.5/4 = 62.5%. Lever (crowbar): effort arm 1.2 m, load arm 0.3 m, VR = 4; load 400 N, effort 125 N; MA = 400/125 = 3.2; efficiency = 3.2/4 = 80%.
characters: Mama Kavata Mutua: adult woman at a homestead near Kitui town, Kitui County; lifts the 20 kg bucket from the 8 m deep well; finds a direct lift exhausting. Mwende: her 10-year-old daughter, mass 30 kg; can lift the bucket with the pulley system by pulling the rope downward with a 125 N effort. The well: hand-dug, 8 m from water surface to ground level; water surface is the 0 m reference. The bucket: 20 kg total mass with water, weight 200 N. The pulley system: fixed pulley on a wooden frame above the well plus a movable pulley on the bucket hook, 2 rope sections support the bucket, efficiency 80%. Mr Otieno: physics teacher (Kisumu) who runs the class investigations and demos; learners work in groups at school (use Nairobi, Mombasa, Rift Valley, Lake Victoria only as side examples, not changing the anchor data). Sack of maize: 50 kg, dragged across the rough dirt yard and smooth concrete floor of the homestead store. Lorry bed: 1.0 m high, 4 m plank ramp. Class tools: PhET Energy Skate Park (L1), pendulum and roller coaster videos (L2), PhET Pendulum Lab (L3), Forces and Motion/friction demo (L7). Food link: the energy Mama Kavata and Mwende use comes from chemical energy in food such as ugali and githeri.
outcome: The bucket gains exactly 1600 J of gravitational potential energy whether it is lifted by hand or with the pulley system, because the same 200 N weight is raised the same 8 m. The pulley does not give extra energy or reduce the work needed; it lets Mwende pull a smaller force of 125 N (instead of 200 N) over a longer rope distance of 16 m (instead of 8 m). The energy comes from the chemical energy in the person's body (from food); 2000 J is put in, 1600 J becomes PE of the bucket, and 400 J (20%) is transferred as heat by friction in the pulleys and rope, so energy is conserved overall and none is destroyed.
conventions: Use g = 10 N/kg everywhere (not 9.8). Weight W = mg in newtons (N). Use KE = 1/2 mv squared and PE = mgh (gravitational potential energy, measured from the water surface at 0 m). Energy and work are in joules (J); power in watts (W), 1 W = 1 J/s; force in N; distance in m; time in s. Work: W = Fd, with F in the direction of motion; positive work when force is in the direction of motion, negative when opposite; work and energy transferred use the same unit. Work-energy link: work done on an object = change in its energy. Conservation of energy: energy is never created or destroyed, only transformed or transferred; 'lost' energy means transferred to the surroundings as heat and sound, never destroyed. Power P = W/t. Machine terms: load (the weight being lifted), effort (the force applied). MA = load/effort (no unit); VR = distance moved by effort/distance moved by load (no unit); efficiency = (useful work output / work input) x 100% = (MA/VR) x 100%. A machine never reduces the work needed; it trades a smaller force for a longer distance. A single fixed pulley changes the direction of force only (MA about 1); the homestead rig uses two pulleys so MA is above 1. Round speeds to 1 decimal place (11.0 for 10.95). Use the words 'pulley system' for the rig in the well.

lessonMap.focus: Kinetic and potential energy: the bucket in the well
lessonMap.teaches: Energy is stored because of position (potential) or present because of motion (kinetic); a lifted bucket stores more potential energy the higher it is. Students also start the DQB and an initial model (qualitative, no formulas yet).
lessonMap.buildsOn: None; launches the phenomenon in Kitui and uses prior knowledge of lifting and falling.
lessonMap.usesData: Bucket PE table (qualitative trend 0 to 1600 J only to show increase), the 20 kg bucket, 8 m well, direct lift versus pulley story; Energy Skate Park observation of PE/KE exchange.

lessonMap.focus: Energy transformations and the formulas KE and PE
lessonMap.teaches: Calculating KE = 1/2 mv squared and PE = mgh and tracing how PE changes into KE and back in a pendulum and roller coaster.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 1: the ideas of potential and kinetic energy and the initial model.
lessonMap.usesData: Pendulum (1 J, 2 m/s), roller coaster (200 000 J, 20 m/s), bucket PE table values 400 to 1600 J, free-fall table PE/KE columns.

lessonMap.teaches: The principle that in an ideal system total energy (KE + PE) stays constant, tested with the pendulum and the free-falling bucket.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 2: calculation of KE and PE and transformations.
lessonMap.usesData: Free-fall table (KE + PE = 1600 J at every height), pendulum bob 1 J, PhET Pendulum Lab.

lessonMap.focus: Conservation of energy in applications and energy losses
lessonMap.teaches: Using conservation of energy to solve problems for falling and sliding objects and accounting for energy lost as heat and sound (real systems).
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 3: total energy constant in ideal systems; Lesson 2: formulas for KE and PE.
lessonMap.usesData: Free-fall table ideal speed 12.6 m/s versus real fall 11 m/s, KE 1210 J, 390 J lost; link back to the bucket.

lessonMap.teaches: Defining work as force times distance in the direction of the force, calculating it, and telling positive from negative work.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1-4: energy as the ability to do work and the unit joule.
lessonMap.usesData: Direct lift 200 N x 8 m = 1600 J; work signs for lifting and lowering the bucket (+1600 J, -1600 J, net 0 J).

lessonMap.focus: Work and energy: hand versus pulley
lessonMap.teaches: Work done on an object equals its change in energy, and comparing hand and pulley work shows smaller force over a longer distance and where the extra input energy goes.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 5: W = Fd and signs; Lesson 3-4: conservation and energy losses; Lesson 1 DQB.
lessonMap.usesData: Hand lift 1600 J; pulley effort 125 N x 16 m = 2000 J input, 1600 J PE, 400 J lost as heat.

lessonMap.teaches: Friction does negative work that must be overcome (work = friction x distance) and power P = W/t measures how fast work is done.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 5-6: W = Fd and energy transfer to heat.
lessonMap.usesData: Sack of maize rough versus smooth (1500 J at 60 W; 1000 J at 50 W), stair climb (250 W and 500 W), water lift 80 W and 100 W input.

lessonMap.focus: Simple machines, MA, VR, efficiency and the final model
lessonMap.teaches: Calculating mechanical advantage, velocity ratio and efficiency for pulleys, levers and ramps and using them to explain how the pulley reduces effort while energy is conserved.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1-7: energy, conservation, work, friction losses and power.
lessonMap.usesData: Pulley system (MA 1.6, VR 2, 80%), fixed pulley VR 1, ramp (2.5, 4, 62.5%), crowbar (3.2, 4, 80%); final outcome of the Kitui bucket.
